title: A current vanishing away from a compact set and on a neighbourhood domain is zero
statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ and B ⊆ U ⊆ ℝ^P with B open, let K ⊆ B be compact, and let F ∈ 𝒟_m(U). Assume F(ω) = 0 for every ω ∈ 𝒟^m(U) whose topological support is disjoint from K, and F(ι ψ) = 0 for every ψ ∈ 𝒟^m(B) (ι = testFormOnInclusion). Then F(ω) = 0 for every ω ∈ 𝒟^m(U).
lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (U B K : Set (Euclid P)) (hBU : B ⊆ U) (F : GeometricCurrentOn U m), IsOpen B → IsCompact K → K ⊆ B → (∀ ω : TestFormOn U m, Disjoint (tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) m)) K → F ω = 0) → (∀ ψ : TestFormOn B m, F (testFormOnInclusion hBU m ψ) = 0) → ∀ ω : TestFormOn U m, F ω = 0
